document.summary: Alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold (AB hydrolase-1) proteins. SF5 holds the gammaproteobacterial biotin pathway esterase BioH (pimeloyl-ACP methyl ester esterase, E. coli P13001) and the Pseudomonas 3-hydroxyacyl transacylases PhaG and RhlA. SF3 holds the B. subtilis stress-signalling protein RsbQ. SF2 holds yeast Lpx1 and diverse bacterial and eukaryotic hydrolases (RutD-like carbamate hydrolases, Rv0045c, RufB). The P. putida KT2440 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q88QE1) is classified in SF2 through its C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain; it adds an N-terminal lipoyl domain.
document.coherence_reason: Members share the fold and serine-hydrolase chemistry, but the characterized activities differ by subfamily: BioH ester hydrolysis in biotin synthesis, PhaG/RhlA acyl transfer in PHA and rhamnolipid synthesis, RsbQ signalling, and Lpx1 lipase activity. Only the broad hydrolase activity is family-wide. The lipoyl-domain acetoin E2s are grouped by NCBIfam NF011457, not by this family.

node_assessments.assessment_reason: Seeded by E. coli BioH but placed on a 17-leaf bacterial node covering all of SF5 and SF3. That node includes B. subtilis RsbQ (SF3), a stress-signalling protein, and within SF5 the P. aeruginosa transacylases PhaG (Q51553) and RhlA (Q51559), whose characterized activity is 3-hydroxyacyl transfer. None of them functions in biotin synthesis. The term is correct for the BioH orthologs that make up most of SF5, so SF5 as a whole is not listed as needing pruning; the transacylase members are recorded as member exceptions on the term assessment below.

document.notes: Node extents come from the PANTHER 19.0 treeinfo API (2026-11-02). PTN002455972 spans SF5 (15 leaves, including P. aeruginosa PhaG and RhlA) and SF3 (RsbQ). PTN002455963 spans SF2 (74) and SF4 (8) under a Eukaryota constraint. PR #5078 carries a machine-generated draft of this file; this curated version supersedes it. SF2 contains the P. putida KT2440 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q88QE1), placed there by its C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain while its N-terminal lipoyl domain carries the E2 role. No GO:0004742 assessment is made: acetyl transfer is a property of that one member, not of SF2's Lpx1-type and RutD-type hydrolases, and a SUBFAMILY_ONLY scope would assert it for all of them. The acetoin module therefore grounds the E2 on NCBIfam NF011457, which groups the lipoyl/alpha-beta-hydrolase acetoin E2s, and records that no PANTHER family describes the E2 role.

document.preferred_name: ABHD6-type monoacylglycerol lipases and related alpha/beta hydrolases
document.summary: An alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold family named for vertebrate ABHD6, a membrane-anchored monoacylglycerol lipase that also associates with AMPA-type glutamate receptors (SF5). Most other members are uncharacterized bacterial, fungal, algal and plant AB hydrolases (SF31, SF33, SF26 and others). The Pseudomonas putida PpG2 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q59695) and the P. putida KT2440 NicD protein are classified in SF33 through their C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain. AcoC adds an N-terminal lipoyl domain and is assigned as a dihydrolipoyllysine-residue acetyltransferase.
document.coherence_reason: The alpha/beta-hydrolase fold is shared, but experimentally supported activities are few and clade-specific: monoacylglycerol lipase for ABHD6 (SF5), and epoxide hydrolase or uracil catabolism for single bacterial seeds. SF33 is a mixture of fungal and algal putative hydrolases plus the lipoyl-domain AcoC. Membrane and lipase assertions seeded by ABHD6 do not hold for the soluble E2 AcoC. The proteobacterial lipoyl/AB-hydrolase acetoin E2s are grouped by NCBIfam NF011457 rather than by any one PANTHER family.

node_assessments.assessment_reason: A single mouse Abhd6 seed places membrane on a 134-leaf node. The node covers almost the whole family: SF5 ABHD6 plus SF33, SF31, SF14, SF26 and other bacterial, fungal and algal hydrolases. ABHD6 has a transmembrane anchor that the soluble bacterial members do not share. TreeGrafter grafts PpG2 AcoC into PTN008685320 under this node. document.notes: Node extents come from the PANTHER 19.0 treeinfo API (2026-11-02). PTN000177089, PTN000863140, PTN002458043 and PTN002463243 appear in this family's PAINT slice but not in its 19.0 tree. The sub-clade PTN008685320 (9 SF33 leaves: diatom, oomycete, green-algal and rice proteins) is the TreeGrafter graft point for PpG2 AcoC and lies under PTN001661081. PR #5078 carries a machine-generated draft of this file; this curated version supersedes it. SF33 contains the P. putida PpG2 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q59695), grafted there by its C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain while its N-terminal lipoyl domain carries the E2 role. No GO:0004742 assessment is made: acetyl transfer is a property of that one member, not of SF33's 60 fungal and algal putative hydrolases, and a SUBFAMILY_ONLY scope would assert it for all of them. The acetoin module therefore grounds the E2 on NCBIfam NF011457, which groups the lipoyl/alpha-beta-hydrolase acetoin E2s, and records that no PANTHER family describes the E2 role.
